column19: During an internship project where we had to deliver a web application, we faced a critical issue. Just two days before the presentation, user authentication suddenly started failing intermittently in production, even though everything was working perfectly in our local environment. My task was to identify and fix this bug urgently without delaying our final submission. Instead of changing the code randomly, I used a structured approach. I isolated the environment by analyzing the production server logs, where I noticed a Token Mismatch error. By digging deeper, I realized that the production environment used a Load Balancer, and user sessions were not being shared across servers. To fix this, I configured a centralized session store using Redis, ensuring all servers shared the same authentication data. The bug was resolved within a few hours. The application became perfectly stable, and we successfully delivered the project on time, receiving excellent feedback from the evaluation panel.

I ran into a Git merge conflict between two branches during a team project. A couple of us had modified the code in a same file, which blocked the project.
My main priority was to quickly resolve it without losing anyone's work. I started by running git status to put in evidence the conflicting files, and then used git diff to see exactly what changed.
Since I wanted to be 100% safe, I actually used an AI assistant to double-check my logic and confirm the commands before running them. I then manually cleaned up the conflicts picked the right versions and put everything together with git add and git commit. I then merge the branch on the main branch
